pr_comments: This will still leave the `turn_on()` service in a broken state since it only checks for the broadcast_address to add the kwargs so if a user only sets a port in their config that will never be passed to the actual `send_magic_packet()` service.  Further it will still log the port giving the user bad debug info.

comments: It looks like port is required, not optional.
I'm having the same issue.  Wake on Lan does not work since the latest update.

Next release will make it optional, but for now, you can fix this by adding manual entry in your config:
`broadcast_port: "9"`
This is a duplicate of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/37107 which also has a PR against it for a fix.

review_comments: The address also requires a default. For both, please use the `DEFAULT_` parameters in the `wakeonlan` package. https://github.com/remcohaszing/pywakeonlan/blob/master/wakeonlan.py

Alternative is to not pass the args at all to the wlan function.

```python
kwargs = {}
if CONF_BROADCAST_PORT in call.data:
    kwargs['port'] = call.data[CONF_BROADCASTPORT]

await hass.async_add_job(
    partial(
        wakeonlan.send_magic_packet,
        mac_address,
        **kwargs,
    )
)
```

btw this is also broken in the `__init__.py` service.

@balloob I have had a PR to fix this as well that sort of takes this approach. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/37387

looks like there might be duplicate issues for the port option addition. I would not default the port in HA but leave that up to the library at this time.
